core_obligations: Invoke the spectral sequence (proof lines 1516-1517): use the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence associated to the covering U and the sheaf F.

Read off the vanishing (proof lines 1518-1519): the hypothesis that H^i of F vanishes on all fibre products U_{i_0} x_U ... x_U U_{i_p} for i > 0 says exactly that E_2^{p,q} = 0 for all q different from 0.

Conclude by degeneration (proof lines 1519-1520): a spectral sequence with only one nonvanishing row degenerates at E_2, so the abutment H^p(U, F) is the E_2^{p,0} term, which is the Cech cohomology of the covering.
proof_roadmap: Take the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence of the given covering.
The hypothesis makes all E_2 terms with q different from 0 vanish.
The spectral sequence therefore degenerates at E_2.
Hence Cech cohomology of the covering agrees with the cohomology of F on U.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives the standard criterion under which Cech cohomology of a covering computes cohomology: if the higher cohomology of F vanishes on every fibre product U_{i_0} x_U ... x_U U_{i_p} of members of the covering, then Cech H^p of the covering equals H^p(U, F) (statement lines 1505-1513). The proof identifies the hypothesis with the vanishing of the E_2 terms of the Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence off the row q = 0, so the spectral sequence degenerates and the abutment is the E_2^{p,0} row (proof lines 1516-1520). The content is the correct reading of the hypothesis into the E_2 page. The claim is H2: one spectral-sequence degeneration, no further construction.
